sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants are in custody since 06.10.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicants are the permanent resident of district and there is no possibility of their absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.
They are ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicants be released on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
Charge-sheet has been filed in this case and bail has been granted to other accused persons including Yogesh Sharma in M.Cr.C. No.54069/2023.
6. According to applicants, they were working as employees in the concerned petrol pump and they have been arrayed as an accused on the basis of memorandum of other accused.
It has also been argued that no recovery has been made from their possession nor any bill signed by them was seized.
7. This bail application has been opposed by the State.
8 . Case diary reveals that no recovery was made from the applicants.

Although, some receipts issued by petrol pump were seized in the matter,
but those documents have not been sent for hand writing examination to show involvement of applicants in the crime.

Further, it has been claimed in the charge-sheet that applicant Vipin Sharma and some other accused persons jointly deposited a part of defalcated amount, but no document regarding this deposit has been seized and filed along with the charge-sheet.

9. Having considered all these facts, this Court finds it appropriate to release the applicants on bail,
therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

10. It is directed that the applicants shall be released on bail upon her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for their appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

11. It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
12.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
